Cyber Attack Disrupts German Steel Industry; thyssenkrupp AG Among Firms Impacted

A large-scale cyber attack targeting Germany’s steel industry has caused significant disruption to operations, with thyssenkrupp AG confirming it is among the companies affected. The incident, which began late Tuesday night, is ongoing and has prompted several firms to halt production and disconnect key IT systems as a precaution.

Industry sources say the attack involved ransomware, with hackers demanding payment to restore access to compromised systems. The German Steel Federation (WV Stahl) stated Wednesday that “multiple major steel producers have suffered IT outages, resulting in curtailed output and logistical delays.” WV Stahl did not provide a precise estimate of the scale but noted that “the impact on the supply chain is severe and could worsen if systems are not restored quickly.”

A spokesperson for thyssenkrupp AG said, “We have taken immediate steps to contain the attack and protect our data. Production processes at several facilities have been temporarily interrupted.” The company did not disclose which plants were affected or comment on ransom demands.

Emil Berger, an analyst with Frankfurt-based Pruessmann Advisory, commented, “The steel sector is highly dependent on digital infrastructure for everything from logistics to process automation. A prolonged outage could lead to material shortages and missed delivery deadlines.”

The IG Metall union urged companies to keep workers informed and ensure wage continuity during the disruption. “It’s vital to safeguard both jobs and safety standards as systems are restored,” said union representative Claudia Henke.

As of Wednesday afternoon, technical teams across the sector are working to assess the full extent of the breach and restore normal operations.
